title: Ethiopian Tomato and Onion Sauce
community: All of Ethiopia — the basic sauce base
author: Mama Tigist
desc: Ethiopian Tomato and Onion Sauce — a base sauce of ripe tomatoes, onions, garlic, and a light touch of spice that underpins many Ethiopian stews. This is the everyday sauce base — used as a starting point for fish stews, vegetable dishes, and lighter preparations.
longDesc: Ethiopian tomato-onion sauce is the universal cooking base — made from tomatoes, onion, and garlic with minimal spice, it is used as the foundation for lighter Ethiopian stews and as a condiment alongside injera.
steps: Heat oil. Cook onion until very golden — 10 minutes.
Add garlic and ginger. Cook 1 minute.
chefTips: Cook this until the tomatoes have fully broken down — not chunky.
cookingScience: Extended cooking of tomatoes concentrates their lycopene (antioxidant), glutamate (umami), and reduces their acidity through evaporation of volatile acids.
sustainabilityTips: A base sauce that enables many other dishes from minimal ingredients.
servedWith: As a base for fish stews, vegetable dishes
As a simple condiment with injera
culturalNote: The Ethiopian tomato-onion sauce is the universal canvas — the base from which dozens of different stews emerge through the addition of berbere, different proteins, or different vegetables.
